properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued October 5 at 7:53PM EDT until October 5 at 8:30PM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
FFWJAX

The National Weather Service in Jacksonville has extended the

* Flash Flood Warning for...
East Central Clay County in northeastern Florida...
Northeastern Putnam County in northeastern Florida...
West Central St. Johns County in northeastern Florida...

* Until 830 PM EDT.

* At 753 PM EDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 2 and 5 inches of rain
have fallen. Additional rainfall amounts up to 0.5 inches are
possible in the warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected
to begin shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Green Cove Springs, Picolata and Bakersville.
properties.instruction:
Turn around, don't drown when encountering flooded roads. Most flood
deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

moving away from the Marshall Islands, with decreasing showers
across the islands and atolls. Winds will remain strong and gusty
through today as far south as Majuro, but are expected to decrease
below Small Craft Advisory levels this afternoon.

more information on Koguma, see bulletins issued by the Joint
Typhoon Warning Center under WMO header WTPN33 PGTW and by the
National Weather Service under WMO header WTPQ33 PGUM.

properties.areaDesc: Coastal Bryan; Coastal Chatham; Coastal Liberty; Coastal McIntosh; Beaufort; Coastal Colleton; Charleston; Coastal Jasper
properties.headline: Rip Current Statement issued October 5 at 7:09PM EDT until October 6 at 8:00PM EDT by NWS Charleston SC
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerous rip currents expected.

* WHERE...South Carolina Beaches, and Georgia Beaches.

* WHEN...From Tuesday morning through Tuesday evening.

* IMPACTS...Rip currents can sweep even the best swimmers away
from shore into deeper water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...High surf with breaking waves of 4 to 6
feet along the lower South Carolina coast and 5 to 7 feet along
the Georgia coast will occur. The combination of strong
northeast winds, elevated tides and large breaking waves will
increase the risk for significant beach erosion. A High Surf
Advisory may be issued for Tuesday and Tuesday night.
properties.instruction:
Swim near a lifeguard. If caught in a rip current, relax and
float. Don't swim against the current. If able, swim in a
direction following the shoreline. If unable to escape, face the

properties.headline: Special Marine Warning issued October 5 at 7:08PM EDT until October 5 at 9:15PM EDT by NWS Tallahassee FL
properties.description:
SMWTAE

The National Weather Service in Tallahassee has issued a

* Special Marine Warning for...
Apalachee Bay or Coastal Waters From Keaton Beach to Ochlockonee
River Fl out to 20 Nm...
Coastal Waters From  Ochlockonee River to Apalachicola FL out to 20
Nm...

* Until 915 PM EDT.

* At 708 PM EDT, a severe thunderstorm capable of producing
waterspouts was located 11 nm northeast of St George Island, moving
northeast at 20 knots.

HAZARD...Waterspouts and wind gusts 34 knots or greater.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Waterspouts can quickly form and capsize boats...damage
vessels...and create suddenly higher waves. Make sure all
on board are in a secure location and wearing life
jackets. Expect wind gusts in excess of 34
knots...suddenly higher waves...frequent lightning...and
heavy downpours. Make sure all on board are wearing life
jackets.

* Locations impacted include...
Marker 24 Barge.
properties.instruction:
Move to safe harbor until hazardous weather passes.

Move to safe harbor immediately as gusty winds and high waves are
expected.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Warning issued October 5 at 3:32PM PDT until October 9 at 8:00PM PDT by NWS Las Vegas NV
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions with high temperatures near 110
degrees and overnight lows only getting down to around 85 degrees.
This will yield at least major Heat Risk, impacting anyone without
adequate cooling and hydration.

* WHERE...Elevations in Death Valley National Park below 2000 feet.

* WHEN...Until 8 PM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Heat-related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events.
properties.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Do not leave young children and pets in unattended vehicles. Car
interiors will reach lethal temperatures in a matter of minutes.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and
loose-fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early
morning or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat
exhaustion and heat stroke.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Monitor the latest forecasts and warnings for updates.

properties.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued October 5 at 2:47PM PDT until October 9 at 11:00PM PDT by NWS Los Angeles/Oxnard CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents
and breaking waves due to elevated surf expected. For the
Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding and elevated surf
expected.

* WHERE...Catalina and Santa Barbara Islands, Ventura County
Beaches, Malibu Coast and Los Angeles County Beaches.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, from Tuesday afternoon
through late Tuesday night. For the Coastal Flood Advisory,
from 6 AM Wednesday to 11 PM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Moderate flooding of sea water is likely over some
vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time
of high tide, including over beach parking lots, bike paths,
and harbor walkways. Moderate beach erosion is likely.
Isolated damage is unlikely but possible. There is an
increased risk of ocean drowning. Rip currents can pull
swimmers and surfers out to sea. Waves can wash people off
beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats nearshore.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Coastal flooding impacts will be greatest
for Long Beach, Catalina Island, Zuma Beach and Malibu.
properties.instruction:
Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone property. Do
NOT drive around barricades or through water of unknown depth.

Remain out of the water due to hazardous swimming conditions, or
stay near occupied lifeguard towers. Rock jetties can be deadly
in such conditions, stay off the rocks.

deaths occur in vehicles.

Be aware of your surroundings and do not drive on flooded roads.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

properties.description:
* WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, dangerous rip currents
expected. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, minor coastal flooding
expected.

* WHERE...San Diego County Coastal Areas and Orange County
Coastal Areas.

* WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, from Tuesday afternoon
through Friday evening. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 6
AM Wednesday to 11 AM PDT Friday.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only isolated
road closures expected. Minor coastal erosion is also expected.

expected to peak between 6.5 and 7.0 feet during the mornings
and evenings.

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Remain out of the water to avoid hazardous swimming conditions.

properties.headline: Extreme Heat Watch issued October 5 at 11:38AM MST until October 8 at 8:00PM MST by NWS Phoenix AZ
properties.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously hot conditions possible. Afternoon temperatures
104 to 108. Major Heat Risk.

* WHERE...Yuma.

* WHEN...From Wednesday morning through Thursday evening.

* IMPACTS...Heat related illnesses increase significantly during
extreme heat events. Overexposure can cause heat cramps and heat
exhaustion to develop and, without intervention, can lead to heat
stroke.
properties.instruction:
An Extreme Heat Watch means that a period of very hot temperatures,
even by local standards, may occur. Actions should be taken to lessen
the impact of the extreme heat.

Take extra precautions if you work or spend time outside. When
possible, reschedule strenuous activities to early morning or
evening. Know the signs and symptoms of heat exhaustion and heat
stroke. Wear lightweight and loose-fitting clothing when possible and
drink plenty of water.

To reduce risk during outdoor work, the Occupational Safety and
Health Administration recommends scheduling frequent rest breaks in
shaded or air conditioned environments. Anyone overcome by heat
should be moved to a cool and shaded location. Heat stroke is an
emergency! Call 9 1 1.

Public cooling shelters are available in some areas. Consult county
officials for more details.

properties.description:
* IMPACTS: Low humidities, unseasonably warm temperatures, and
gusty winds will create erratic fire behavior and rapid fire
spread.

* AFFECTED AREA:
In South Central MT Fire Zones...123...124.

* COUNTIES AFFECTED:
In Central MT...Wheatland.
In South Central MT...Park...Sweet Grass.
In Southwest MT...Gallatin.

* WIND: West 10 to 20 mph with gusts up to 35 mph.

* HUMIDITY: As low as 12 percent.

* TEMPERATURES: Up to 87.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS: The worst conditions are expected across
the lower to mid elevations in fine fuels.
properties.instruction:
A Red Flag Warning means that critical fire weather conditions are
either occurring now, or will shortly. A combination of gusty
winds, low relative humidity, and unseasonably warm temperatures
can contribute to extreme fire behavior.

properties.headline: Heat Advisory issued October 5 at 9:29AM PDT until October 8 at 10:00PM PDT by NWS San Francisco CA
properties.description:
* WHAT...Hot conditions with maximum temperatures in the mid-90s to
near 105. Mild minimum temperatures and weak onshore flow will
limit overnight relief.

* WHERE...The East Bay and San Francisco Bay Shoreline, North Bay
Interior Mountains and Valleys, The Santa Clara Valley and Eastern
Hills, The Santa Cruz Mountains, Interior Monterey County and the
Santa Lucia Range, Most of San Benito County and the Cholame Hills
in Southeast Monterey County, and Southern Salinas Valley/Arroyo
Seco and Lake San Antonio.

* WHEN...Until 10 PM PDT Thursday.

* IMPACTS...This level of heat affects anyone without effective
cooling and/or adequate hydration. Impacts likely in some health
systems, heat-sensitive industries and infrastructure.
properties.instruction:
Hydration is a critical piece to surviving the heat. Drink water, and
if possible, take water to those who are vulnerable.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to the early
morning or evening. Take action when you experience symptoms of heat
exhaustion and/or heat stroke.

Beat the heat and check the backseat! Do not leave young children or
pets in unattended vehicles. Car interiors will reach lethal
temperatures in a matter of minutes.

properties.areaDesc: Baker, FL; Nassau, FL; Charlton, GA
properties.headline: Flood Warning issued October 5 at 10:03AM EDT by NWS Jacksonville FL
properties.description:
...The Flood Warning continues for the following rivers in Georgia...
Florida...

St Mary's River At Macclenny affecting Charlton, Baker and Nassau
Counties.

Additional information is available at
https://water.weather.gov/wfo/JAX

The next statement will be issued Tuesday morning at 1015 AM EDT.

* WHAT...Minor flooding is forecast.

* WHERE...St Mary's River at Macclenny.

* WHEN...Until further notice.

* IMPACTS...At 12.0 feet, Minor flooding of low lying areas and
timber lands including some properties along St. Mary's River Bluff
Road and the Cypress Landing Resort on the Georgia side. At 14.0
feet, Flooding of bottomlands along the river and some lower access
roads including the lower half of St. Mary's River Bluff Road which
cuts off 15 to 20 homes on the Georgia side. At 15.0 feet, Flooding
begins to impact the lower end of Steel Bridge Road on the Florida
side and cuts off access to the river gage as well as access to
several homes. At 16.0 feet, Access roads on both sides of the
river in Florida and Georgia are flooded, including the entire low
lying stretch of St. Mary's River Bluff Road on the Georgia side
which cuts off 40 to 50 homes. On the Florida side, the lower end
of St. Mary's Cove Road past the public boat ramp becomes flooded
and cuts off access to 20 to 30 homes. The Stokes Road Bridge over
the river is generally closed due to high water.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- At 9:45 AM EDT Monday the stage was 12.0 feet.
- Forecast...The river is expected to rise to a crest of 14.0 feet
tomorrow evening.
- Flood stage is 12.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

may already be occurring. Persons along rivers and streams in the
warned area should take immediate precautions to protect life and
property.

These forecasts are based almost entirely on observed precipitation
as little to no additional precipitation is currently expected over
the next 24 to 48 hours.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov.

The next statement will be issued by this evening.

properties.areaDesc: Majuro Coastal Waters
properties.headline: Special Weather Statement issued October 5 at 10:24AM ChST by NWS Tiyan GU
properties.description:
UPDATED to account for Invest 94W becoming TD 27W.

...HEAVY SHOWERS, GUSTY WINDS, AND CHOPPY SEAS LIKELY THE NEXT FEW
DAYS ACROSS THE NORTHERN MARSHALL ISLANDS DOWN TO MAJURO...

A developing disturbance known as Invest 94W by the Joint Typhoon
Warning Center (JTWC) is located about 140 miles southwest of
Utirik. Scatterometry data indicates 15 to 20 kt winds near
Kwajalein, Ebadon, Ujae, Bikini, and Rongelap, with winds up to 25 kt
near heavier showers. TD 27W will be generally slow to move,
remaining over the northern Marshall Islands through Tuesday night.
Scattered to numerous showers and isolated thunderstorms may lead to
locally heavy rainfall and flooding. Through Friday, 4 to 6 inches of
rain with locally higher amounts are possible.

Gusty winds and elevated, choppy seas will make marine conditions
difficult. Residents may need to reconsider plans for inter-island
boating as the week continues.

27W will continue to develop near Kwajalein over the next day or
two, so residents in the northern Republic of Marshall Islands (RMI)
should monitor the forecast for the next several days.

For more information on Invest 94W please see the Significant Tropical
Weather Advisory from the Joint Typhoon Warning Center under WMO
header ABPW10 PGTW. Also keep up to date with the latest information
from your local emergency management agency.
